subject: deathstalker scorpion
title: Doctors Use a Deadly Scorpion's Venom to Find Brain Tumours

scenes.text: One of the most dangerous scorpions is helping surgeons save lives.
It's the deathstalker, from North Africa and the Middle East.
Its venom holds a protein called chlorotoxin that sticks to tumour cells and leaves healthy ones alone.
Scientists in Seattle attached a glowing dye to a copy of it.
Under near-infrared light, the tumour glows, so surgeons can see exactly where to cut.
Children with brain tumours were among the first patients. The deathstalker's weapon became a flashlight.

description:
A protein from deathstalker scorpion venom, chlorotoxin, sticks to tumour cells, and scientists turned it into a glowing tumour paint.
Developed by Jim Olson's team at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center, it makes tumours light up under near-infrared light; it has been tested in clinical trials, including on children with brain tumours.
What other venom do you think could become medicine?
first_comment: Cone snail venom also became a painkiller. Which venomous animal would you least want to meet?
